# Run book: Check which rights an endpoint needs

[Run books](README.md) | [User guide](../user-guide/check-your-rights.md) | [Spec](../specs/check-your-rights.md)

## Contents

- [Purpose](#purpose)

- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Purpose

See the authorization model in one place: anonymous, authenticated or application rights, the same on every API surface.

## Preconditions

- The example API is running.

## Verify

Automatically: `npx playwright test e2e/journeys.spec.ts -g "Check which rights an endpoint needs"` (add `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8088` to run against the compose stack).

By hand, in the example web application at `/identity/rights`:

1. **Read the endpoint table.** Every endpoint is listed with its access. The filter narrows the list to a route or a right. Expect: The table lists the rights.demo endpoint with access rights.
2. **Check a right.** Check asks the host whether the current user holds at least one of the listed rights. Expect: A result is shown with the rights the user holds.

## Troubleshooting

**Table 1 — Known problems**

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The check says Unauthenticated | The host runs anonymously or the token is missing | Sign in, then check again |
| The check says Forbidden | The token has none of the listed rights | Ask for a role that is translated to one of the rights |

Related framework features: OoBDev.AspNetCore.Abstractions (`[ApplicationRight]`, `IApplicationRightChecker`).
